title: Fashion Revolution
tagline: She strips away the corsets and dresses an entire century in freedom.

scenes.text: Paris, 1910. Women are still wearing whalebone corsets, suffocating layers of skirts, and hats the size of carriages. A milliner from Aubazine with a sharp eye and sharper tongue is about to liberate the female body — one design at a time.

scenes.speaker: Coco Chanel
scenes.text: Fashion is not something that exists only in dresses. Fashion is in the sky, in the street. It has to do with ideas, the way we live, what is happening. The corset was a prison. I opened the door.

challenge.instruction: Chanel is moving her hats from Balsan's flat to her own shop at 21 rue Cambon. Carry the stack of hatboxes across without crushing a single hat.
challenge.fact: Chanel's first success was hats: plain straw boaters stripped of the feathers and fruit then in fashion. When the actress Gabrielle Dorziat wore them on the Paris stage in 1912, the city followed.

scenes.text: Chanel didn't just change clothes — she changed what elegance meant. Before Chanel, simplicity was poverty. After Chanel, simplicity was sophistication. The little black dress, the collarless jacket, jersey fabric — all revolutionary in their time.

challenge.instruction: Simplicity still has to be made by hand. Set up the workrooms so each jersey dress moves from cutting to finishing without a bottleneck.
challenge.fact: Each of Chanel's innovations stripped away constraint. Jersey replaced stiff silk; cardigan suits replaced corsets; black replaced colour as the dominant fashion statement. She built freedom into fashion at a time when clothing was still architecture built to restrict women's bodies.

scenes.speaker: Coco Chanel
scenes.text: I don't do fashion. I am fashion. And Chanel No. 5 — I wanted a woman's perfume that smells like a woman, not like a flower or like a lily of the valley. Something complex. Something that requires thought.

challenge.instruction: The Jazz Age inspired Chanel's Paris salon. Arrange the notes of a 1920s jazz phrase.
challenge.fact: Chanel thrived in the Jazz Age Paris of the 1920s — a world of Picasso, Stravinsky, Diaghilev, and Hemingway. She dressed the dancers of the Ballets Russes and set the aesthetic for an entire era.

challenge.instruction: Chanel built an empire on her own terms and watched every franc of it. Make the house accounts add up.
challenge.fact: Victorian corsets could pull a waist to 45 cm (18 inches), causing fainting, rib deformities, and displaced organs. Chanel borrowed fabrics from men's sportswear — jersey, tweed — and designed for movement. 'I gave women a sense of freedom,' she said. 'I gave them back their bodies.' It was a cultural revolution sewn into cloth.

scenes.speaker: Coco Chanel
scenes.text: This time the whole board is judged at once. Deploy Itō Hirobumi, George Bernard Shaw and me, turn us public, then declare the Auction: the highest public Wealth on the board when the round ends takes the prize.

challenge.instruction: Fight lesson 6 · Global Competition. Deploy your Great People, Go Public on each, then start the Auction and End Turn to win the round with the highest public Wealth on the board.
challenge.fact: A Global Competition counts every public Great Person on the whole board; followers and face-down cards add nothing. It lasts one round, and the strongest player draws a reward: event cards, followers or a new Great Person.
